activity.notes: Maya inscriptions give Spearthrower Owl an accession in 374 and death in 439, and identify him as father of the Teotihuacan-linked Tikal ruler Yax Nuun Ahiin I. David Stuart's 2024 synthesis argues that he was a historical ruler of Teotihuacan. The personal dates are epigraphically grounded, but identifying his unspecified throne with Teotihuacan remains a scholarly reconstruction rather than an uncontested contemporary title; ATLAS therefore records the polity link with confidence 'likely'.

sources.title: David Stuart, Spearthrower Owl: A Teotihuacan Ruler in Maya History
sources.citation_text: The 2024 Dumbarton Oaks monograph argues from epigraphic and iconographic evidence that Spearthrower Owl was a historical ruler of Teotihuacan from 374 to 439 CE.

sources.title: David Stuart, The Arrival of Strangers
sources.citation_text: Stuart's epigraphic discussion identifies an accession date in 374 and a recorded death in 439 while noting that the throne's location must be reconstructed from the Teotihuacan context.
